findings.title: Each sub-flusher process creates its own separate SpansBuffer and Redis connections
findings.body: _create_process_for_shards creates a new SpansBuffer(shards) per process and multiple processes now share the same backing Redis, but each gets its own connection pool / client. With many processes per consumer (num_processes shards split across up to flusher_processes), this multiplies Redis connections significantly beyond what one buffer-per-consumer used before, which can exhaust Redis maxclients under scale-up scenarios the PR is explicitly targeting (scaling down consumers but relying on more flusher processes).

findings.title: join() deadline handling can let a process be killed/skipped silently without raising
findings.body: In join(), the loop `for process_index, process in self.processes.items(): if deadline is not None: remaining_time = deadline - time.time(); if remaining_time <= 0: break` just breaks out of the whole loop once the deadline is exceeded for any single process, leaving the remaining processes neither waited-on nor terminated. Previously there was only one process so this corner case didn't exist; now, with multiple processes, some may be left running (not terminated) if the deadline is hit partway through, leaking subprocesses after shutdown of the strategy pipeline step and continuing to write to Kafka/Redis after the main process intends to be done with this instance's lifecycle (e.g. during rebalance restarts) causing duplicate/zombie flusher activity until the whole consumer process exits.

findings.title: max_processes default silently falls back to shard count causing non-deterministic process count across runs with varying partitions
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means if `max_processes=0` is passed, it is treated as falsy and replaced by shard count, which could be surprising/undocumented behavior (0 should probably mean "zero processes" or raise, not fall back silently). This isn't tested and could mask configuration bugs where `flusher_processes=0` is passed unintentionally via CLI defaulting weirdly.

findings.title: process.kill() only guarded for multiprocessing.Process, silently no-ops for Thread
findings.body: In _ensure_processes_alive, `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): process.kill()` means that when running in testing mode where processes are threading.Thread (produce_to_pipe set), an unhealthy/dead thread is never killed (threads can't be killed) but also _create_process_for_shards is still called to spawn a replacement, potentially leaving the old hung thread running indefinitely alongside the new one, leading to duplicate flush activity in tests using produce_to_pipe mode if a thread were ever detected unhealthy.
